purpose: Can a structure-activated gate B_eff = B(phi)*G(X_local) rescue the disformal amplitude channel excluded by 29-1?
model: u_i = G(dphi_i) * u_bar_i; ambient G(0)=0 restores the conformal map; intra-well contrast supplies Delta_v

consistency.interpretation: The three required gate slopes agree within a factor 1.60 per e-fold of depth. A single monotone log/saturating gate predicts equal slopes; the residual ~50% scatter (dominated by J1332) is the consistency budget of a common G(dphi).

ordering_caveat: Parent depths {5.5e-9, 1.05e-8, 4.67e-8} interleave with feature depths {1.81e-8, 3.46e-8, 1.48e-7}: a monotone u(dphi) makes the per-sightline baselines differ, which is admissible (each sightline's uniform level is absorbed by its own redshift anchor) but removes any common-level statement.

population_bound.note: To avoid >few x 10^3 km/s internal disformal displacements in structures deeper than the DLA hosts (clusters at delta_phi ~ 1e-5), the gate must saturate: G(1e-5) <~ few x 1e-3 / u_bar. A saturating activation with G_max ~ 1e-3 / u_bar satisfies this; a steep non-saturating gate would reopen the exclusion at cluster depths.

verdict: PARTIALLY VIABLE. A structure-activated coupling B_eff = B(phi)*G(X_local) with G closed in the ambient and saturating at G ~ 1e-3 inside nonlinear wells restores the ambient redshift map (u_ambient = 0) while supplying the intra-well u-contrasts the three sightlines require. The required gate slopes agree across sightlines within a factor ~1.6 — neither a clean fit nor an exclusion — and the mechanism converts the spectroscopic result into a measurable functional requirement on the disformal sector. Present-day environments are automatically protected by the small-field suppression of the tracked B form (phi_total ~ delta_phi << phi_c), so Cassini/GW170817 bounds are untouched. The channel is therefore NOT excluded in principle but requires a beyond-B(phi) coupling: the disformal sector must be environment-activated, a D2(phi,X)-class generalisation beyond the purely field-tracking forms tested so far.
